summary: Add targeted constructed-response practice for vector subtraction and signed components, plus a short method clarification for directions outside the first quadrant.

improvements.why: Practice is dominated by MCQs and numeric answers; the syllabus explicitly asks learners to add and subtract coplanar vectors, but no learner-drawn construction is assessed.
improvements.what: A Sketch item: draw two non-perpendicular coplanar vectors head to tail, then construct and label their difference by reversing the subtracted vector; award marks for arrow direction and resultant from first tail to last head.

improvements.why: Current component practice mostly uses first-quadrant angles; it does not test the sign and direction of a component when the vector points left or down.
improvements.what: A structured Determine item with a vector pointing up-left at a stated angle to the leftward horizontal; obtain signed horizontal and vertical components and state the resultant direction from a named axis. Include a distractor or marking point for quadrant choice rather than relying on inverse tangent alone.

improvements.where: note, after the resolving equations in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: The displayed equations and inverse-tangent method are written for a vector above the positive horizontal, but the method later asks learners to use signed components generally.
improvements.what: Add a brief note that $F_x=F\cos\theta$ and $F_y=F\sin\theta$ take signs from the chosen axes, and $\tan^{-1}(F_y/F_x)$ needs a quadrant check; name the final direction relative to a stated axis. Add one up-left numerical mini-example without altering existing text.
